solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shoot commercials over by entrance to major conference venue

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game

indicators.note: over tells us to turn the commercials word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: ads are advertisements

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its opening letter, here of major

explanation.surface: Instructions to film adverts near the door of a big meeting hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ADS into SDA. Potsdam, near Berlin, hosted the 1945 Allied conference.
explanation.definitionFit: The German city hosted the famous 1945 meeting of Allied leaders, so it is a historic summit location.

clue.text: Leader of House gets installed in seat — what a relief!

indicators.note: gets installed in means is placed inside the seat word

parts.note: a pew is a church bench, a seat

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of House

explanation.surface: The Leader of the House sighs as they finally get a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an exclamation of relief, uttered after escaping something unpleasant.

clue.text: Sweet substance a chameleon originally left in woody plant?

indicators.note: in places the three small pieces inside the plant word

parts.note: a tree is a woody plant

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of chameleon

explanation.surface: A chameleon leaves something sticky on a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is the thick sweet syrup made in refining sugar, what Americans call molasses.

clue.text: Follow graduate's code of beliefs

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: Instructions to adopt a graduate's set of principles.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a fixed set of principles laid down by an authority as true.

clue.text: Sadly not Henry's first time for the cooler

indicators.note: sadly means things have gone badly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the words not and time as written, plus the first letter of Henry's

explanation.surface: Henry, sadly, did not come first this time for the cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges NOT, H and TIME. A monteith is a scalloped bowl in which wine glasses were cooled.
explanation.definitionFit: A monteith is a large ornamental bowl filled with iced water to chill wine glasses, so a cooler.

clue.text: Disorganised old citizen retiring after tea

indicators.note: after places the retiring piece behind the tea word

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters for old citizen are read backwards

parts.note: cit is a short form of citizen

explanation.surface: A muddled pensioner heads off to bed once tea is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses CITO to give OTIC, which follows CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chaotic is in a state of confusion, lacking any order or organisation.

clue.text: On telephone, stop money order

indicators.note: on the telephone, words are only heard, so a homophone is needed

parts.note: to check something is to stop it

explanation.surface: Cancelling a payment instruction by phoning the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque is a written instruction to a bank to pay money, so an order for money.

clue.text: Folly bust dairy, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately signals things gone wrong, so the letters of bust dairy are jumbled

explanation.surface: Running a dairy into bankruptcy was sheer foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurdity and folly are synonyms for foolish, senseless behaviour.

clue.text: Carry around not quite all of every toasted bun

indicators.note: around means the carry word goes round the shortened piece

parts.note: to take is to carry

indicators.note: not quite all of means the every word loses its last letter

parts.note: each means every

explanation.surface: Bring along nearly everything for a toasted snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry' looks like the start of an instruction but is just the outer word; 'not quite all of' trims the last letter and 'around' wraps the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a light, flat bun with dried fruit, usually served toasted and buttered.

clue.text: Scot's scam squeezing Welshman and male compatriot, say

definitions.note: possessive, read as an adjective meaning Scottish

indicators.note: squeezing means pressing the Welsh name inside the scam word

parts.note: a con is a scam
Aled is a Welsh male name
Ian is a typical Scottish male name, so a compatriot of the Scot

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's swindle traps a Welshman and a fellow Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeezing' puts the Welsh name inside the scam. 'say' marks Ian as just one example of a Scottish name; 'Scot's' is the definition, meaning Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia was the Roman name for Scotland, so Caledonian means Scottish, belonging to a Scot.

clue.text: Disclosure of major crisis mostly dire in the end

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the crisis word loses its final letter

parts.note: an emergency is a major crisis

indicators.note: in the end points to the last letter of dire

explanation.surface: Revealing a big disaster, which mostly turned out dreadful in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the Y from EMERGENCY, leaving EMERGENC.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergence is a coming into view or becoming known, which is a kind of disclosure.

clue.text: Delay getting seat in choir

definitions.meaning: to play for time or hold things up
one of the fixed seats in a church choir

explanation.surface: Stalling while finding a place to sit among the singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalling means delaying, and choir stalls are the enclosed seats in a chancel.

clue.text: Holiday accommodation ultimately rented by male French writer

indicators.note: by means beside, so the last letter of rented sits next to the male name

parts.note: a chateau, a French country house, can be rented for a holiday
Brian is a male first name

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so we take the final letter of rented

explanation.surface: A French author whose holiday home was let to a man.
explanation.walkthrough: François-René de Chateaubriand was a French Romantic writer and statesman; the steak is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Chateaubriand was a leading French Romantic author, known for his memoirs and novels.

clue.text: Simpleton finally given reduced earnings on deck

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of given
reduced means the earnings word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: income is earnings
a poop is the raised deck at a ship's stern

explanation.surface: A fool ends up with a pay cut while working on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is a foolish, stupid person, the same as a simpleton.

clue.text: Name of one with no trust initially in God?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in puts those two letters inside the word for God

parts.note: a deity is a god

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of no and trust

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about believing in a god without any faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives NT, which goes 'in' DEITY to make DENTITY.
explanation.definitionFit: One's identity is who one is, as given by one's name on documents.

clue.text: Is leaving this beneath Queen's old newspaper

indicators.note: leaving means the letters of Is depart from this

parts.note: taken as written
under means beneath
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Something sounding like a royal note left under an old paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thunderer was a nickname for The Times, the paper this puzzle appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times was long nicknamed the Thunderer for its forceful editorials, so it is an old paper's name.

clue.text: Possible carrier's responsibility?

definitions.meaning: a carrier ... delivers messages, so this bird may be a carrier
in the idiom 'not my ...', the word means one's concern or business

explanation.surface: Wondering whose job it is to carry something.
explanation.definitionFit: Some homing birds carry messages, and the idiom 'that's not my pigeon' uses the word for one's own concern.

clue.text: Fighting hard in capturing head of legion

indicators.note: capturing means the batting word takes in the legion letter

parts.note: in cricket, the side that is in is batting

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of legion

explanation.surface: Struggling to seize the commander of a Roman legion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is the cricket term: the team in is batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Battling means struggling vigorously, so putting up a hard fight.

clue.text: Bony protuberance in hornbill caught like that in Paris

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
as means like
que is French for that

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's note on a hornbill caught, with a French phrase thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: A casque is the helmet-like bony growth on top of a hornbill's beak; the word also means a helmet.

clue.text: Cut short Hamlet's rest?

definitions.meaning: Hamlet's dying words are 'the rest is ...'

explanation.surface: A director trims the end of Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Silencing someone interrupts them, and Hamlet's final line ends 'the rest is silence'.

clue.text: Unknown in top pub, a very large rodent

indicators.note: in puts the unknown letter between the top and pub words

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
a bar is a pub
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Something odd in the best pub: a huge rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American capybara is the largest living rodent.

clue.text: Feeler put out by worker upset girl

indicators.note: by means next to, joining the two pieces

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the girl's name reads backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An insect worker sends out a feeler after upsetting a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an insect's sensory organ, the feeler it extends to sense its surroundings.

clue.text: Amusing lass like Candida, for example?

parts.note: fun means amusing
a gal is a girl or lass

explanation.surface: A girl as funny as Shaw's heroine Candida.
explanation.walkthrough: Candida reads as a girl's name, the title heroine of Shaw's play, but here it is the yeast that causes thrush.
explanation.definitionFit: Candida is a yeast, a fungus, so it is described by the adjective for fungi.

clue.text: Social awkwardness of a youth (not women) in Montana

indicators.note: in places the young-man phrase inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: MT is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Montana
a lad is a youth
just men means only males, with no women

explanation.surface: A boy in an all-male Montana setting struggles to fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not women)' is read as JUST MEN, a phrase, not as a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladjustment is failure to adapt to one's surroundings, shown as awkwardness with other people.

clue.text: Young swimmer always seen around lake

indicators.note: around means the always word surrounds the lake letter

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A youngster who is forever swimming laps of the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a fish that swims upriver from the sea.

clue.text: Paid actor supplying cues

definitions.meaning: the straight man who gives a comedian lines to set up the jokes

explanation.surface: A professional actor feeding lines to a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is whimsical: to be fee'd is to have been paid a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: In comedy, the stooge who sets up the punchlines is the feed, and fee'd means paid a fee.

clue.text: One who has depressing experience losing daughter

indicators.note: losing means the daughter letter is dropped from the depressing word

parts.note: a downer is something depressing

explanation.surface: Someone having a miserable time after losing their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who possesses something, so one who has it.

clue.text: Complaint of elderly relative that is opposed to entering church

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the two short pieces go inside the relative word

parts.note: gran is a grandmother
ie abbreviates id est, that is
v stands for versus, against
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A grandmother's grumble about being against going to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' sends both short abbreviations into the relative together; the church abbreviation then goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance is a cause for complaint, a wrong someone feels they have suffered.

clue.text: Like serous membrane — more than one, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is to be heard, giving a homophone

parts.note: plural means more than one

explanation.surface: A medical note on a membrane that seems to come in several parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The pleura is the serous membrane around the lungs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleural means relating to the pleura, a serous membrane lining the chest.

clue.text: Young woman crossing river with festoon of flowers

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the young woman word goes round the river letter

parts.note: gal is informal for a girl
and means with or plus

explanation.surface: A girl wading across a stream carrying a string of blossoms.
explanation.definitionFit: A garland is a wreath or chain of flowers hung as decoration.
